findings.text: Scheduler hotplug hooks manage outgoing and incoming CPUs: deactivation coordinates admission refusal with subsystem teardown while blocking fresh placement, dying validates evacuation and stops per-CPU services, starting restores tick and load state, and waiting blocks until migration completes.

NUMA scheduling helpers publish and withdraw CPU membership in level indexed node masks, derive topology class and distance tables excluding one offline node, detect overridden distance functions, and tear down published state with delayed reclamation plus saved-topology restoration.

Cache-sharing identity management exposes mutex guarded release that clears outgoing CPU ownership and recycles an identifier only when no sibling sharing that cache still claims it, shrinking the tracked maximum when the highest value becomes free.

Deadline bandwidth control exposes offline admission checks, server stop and detach and parameter-update operations, and inspection of attached server reservations, keeping domain totals and runqueue utilization consistent and reporting admission overflow as busy.

Boot constructors initialize symmetric multiprocessing domains, realtime and deadline per-CPU masks, deferrable servers, granularity scaling, NUMA state, and cache and asymmetry tracking, leaving domains built and multiprocessing marked initialized.

Topology classification yields direct when few NUMA levels exist; otherwise it considers the furthest separated pair of CPU nodes and selects mesh when an intermediate node is strictly closer to both, backplane when none exists, and direct as safe fallback on failure.

Recorded NUMA distances hold each distinct valid distance exactly once in increasing order while excluding a designated offline node; any distance outside the architected local to maximum range aborts recording without publication.

Reset returns global NUMA level, distance maximum and topology kind to empty and direct defaults, unpublishes distance and mask pointers, reclaims prior allocations only after a grace period, and restores saved domain topology when present.

Offline admission models the target CPU as already absent by removing its capacity, discounts attached server reservations that will migrate away, skips refusal when no residual deadline reservation remains, and refuses offline when reservations would exceed remaining capacity or no CPU would remain.

Server bandwidth attachment and detachment stay symmetric with CPU activity: detachment stops an active server and withdraws runqueue utilization while touching domain totals only for active CPUs, leaving inactive CPUs to be republished by a later rebuild.

Base slice scales with online CPU count capped at a small bound through a tunable policy selecting constant, linear, or logarithmic growth, recomputed during initialization and whenever the load balance horizon refreshes.

Domain topology mutation, cache identity recycling, cache awareness toggling, and boot domain construction require the domains mutex; cache activation additionally requires CPUs held, and identity release asserts mutex ownership.

Deadline domain totals change under the domain bandwidth lock with scheduler read protection and interrupts masked; server teardown and dying-CPU checks run under runqueue lock, NUMA teardown uses ordered unpublication plus grace-period wait, and deactivation inserts a barrier so new placements observe inactivity.

NUMA scheduling state comprises a compact ordered distance vector whose length equals the level count and a two dimensional mask table indexed by level then node, each entry holding the CPUs considered within that distance threshold for that node.

Asymmetry tracking holds an ordered set of distinct capacity values each paired with a CPU span, linked for safe concurrent traversal with deferred reclamation, collapsing when the machine proves symmetric or a group becomes unpopulated.

An outgoing CPU moves from active to inactive with pushback, then through runqueue offline and subsystem deactivation toward a dying state demanding evacuation to a single unpinned context, finishing with load folding, interval refresh, and timer clearing.

Each deferrable server moves from uninitialized to attached deferrable with cleared runtime, may become active on its runqueue, and returns to inactive detached through stop plus utilization withdrawal, with bandwidth restored only on later attach or rebuild for active CPUs.

Cache aware scheduling has a hardware presence gate and a user enabled active gate: absent hardware forces inactive, otherwise the active gate follows user control, recomputed on domain builds and boot.

Multiprocessor boot entry establishes NUMA state, randomness, domains under lock, init placement on housekeeping CPUs, granularity, realtime and deadline classes, and deferrable servers before marking multiprocessing initialized; domain construction allocates scratch masks, refreshes topology and asymmetry, builds from the housekeeping filtered map, and configures cache awareness.

Failure modes include allocation exhaustion during distance recording and domain or mask setup, invalid distance values, deadline overflow vetoing CPU offline, a dying CPU retaining queued or pinned work with diagnostic output, unclassified topology falling back to direct, and configuration dependent no-op variants for extension, NUMA, and cache helpers.
Default deferrable server reservation uses fifty milliseconds runtime per one second period, establishing a five percent bandwidth share at boot.
Maximum load balance interval scales as online CPU count divided by ten ticks, and granularity scaling caps effective CPU count at eight.
